title: Crash on MacOS when using switch-case fallthrough on Compatibility/any OpenGL renderer in a shader
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5.1.stable, 4.6.beta2[551ce8d47], 3.2.alpha1, 3.2.stable, 3.6.2.stable (any version I've tested *with* switch case support seems to be crashing)

### System information

Godot v4.6.beta2 - macOS Tahoe (26.2.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M4 - Apple M4 (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

When writing a shader and adding any block of code that does a case fallthrough in a switch statement:

```glsl
switch (variable) {
    case 0:
    case 1:
        break;
}
```

The shader is accepted as valid syntax and tries to compile, but whenever that switch statement is actually run in the shader (for example, if you put it in the `light()` function it only crashes when a light is applied to the scene), the entire editor and project crashes.

I wouldn't expect this to crash, especially as it doesn't on other rendering modes (because they don't use OpenGL from what I can tell, since in earlier Godot where it was all Godot it always crashed).

### Steps to reproduce

* Create a shader with a switch case using fallthrough that will run when applied to a `CanvasItem`
* Apply a `ShaderMaterial` using that shader to any `CanvasItem` in any scene
* Watch the editor crash immediately
